android_mechanism: Per-row metadata recomputed on every access; fix computes it once
bug_description: The listening-history page stores each entry as a JSON string and calls JSON.parse(item) four times per row inside the build (cover image URL, name, creator, and click params). Every render of the history list re-parses every entry's JSON four times, wasting UI-thread CPU and growing linearly with history length (plus re-parses on every list mutation).
fix_summary: The item list is mapped to parsed objects once per render and rows read the parsed fields; deletion re-serializes only the affected entry.

test_oracle.definition: Sampled retired-instruction period sum (hw-instructions) attributed to the app process in the complete externally driven measured window.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: Clean captures are valid, but the required 1.2x performance improvement is not met; this case is not accepted.

mechanism_oracle.definition: UI-thread CPU time from page-show to last row rendered plus the re-render after one deletion, from the ace trace.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed performs 4*history_size JSON.parse calls per render (visible in JS sampling); fixed performs history_size parses. unfixed_render_cpu_ms > fixed by >= 25% with 30+ entries.

legacy_instrumented_evidence.note: 600 vs 200 JSON.parse calls per history-page render (mechanism counter, authoritative); whole-step hw-instruction medians are flat (714M vs 695M) because fixed still parses a large baseline, so the declared metric needs a narrower region to separate (measurements-staging).

reproduction: Prepare the external workload fixtures; never apply measurement patches to the app.
Install each clean signed variant and run the PerfLoad_ytmusic_0020 HapRay testcase for >= 3 rounds.
Verify the real UI path and compare the declared CPU/memory metric; build/smoke success alone is not a performance verdict.
